title: Optional: Recent Advances (2022–2026) — The Manifold Hypothesis and the Geometry of Data
content: Overview Imagine a single high-resolution photograph of a human face—say, MATH pixels in color. Formally, that image is a single point living inside a three-million-dimensional Euclidean space MATH . If faces actually scattered uniformly through that colossal void, no machine-learning algorithm in the history of the universe could ever gather enough samples to recognize a smile—the famous curse of dimensionality would swallow every model whole. Yet modern AI recognizes faces, folds proteins, and steers robots effortlessly. Why? Because real-world data almost never fill the ambient space MATH . Instead, they hug a thin, gracefully curved, low-dimensional sheet MATH embedded inside MATH —an idea known as the Manifold Hypothesis . This optional lesson does not replace the foundations you just studied in Chapter 00. Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, topology, and differential equations remain the indispensable alphabet; what follows is a postcard from 2022–2026 showing how that "dry" alphabet has become the living language of statistical manifold theory Whiteley–Gray–Rubin-Delanchy , Geometric Deep Learning Bronstein–Bruna–Cohen–Veličković , and Information Geometry the Fisher–Rao metric . --- Key ideas: Where Does Chapter 00 Meet Modern Data Science? If you graduated in math, computer science, or engineering, you may have learned Jacobians, inner products, and probability distributions in completely separate courses. Here is how they lock together in modern geometry of data. 1. Smooth Manifolds & Embeddings: Sheets Inside Giant Spaces What is it? A MATH -dimensional manifold MATH is a space that looks locally like flat Euclidean space MATH just as Earth looks flat in your neighborhood even though it is a curved sphere . An embedding MATH bends and places that MATH -dimensional sheet inside a much larger ambient space MATH without self-intersections. What does it study? - Intrinsic vs. extrinsic distance: Two points on a rolled-up sheet of paper can sit millimeters apart in 3D space extrinsic chord distance yet centimeters apart if you walk along the paper intrinsic geodesic distance . - Charts and atlases: Stitching local flat coordinate patches together to describe a globally curved space—the exact blueprint behind manifold-learning algorithms like Isomap, UMAP, and t-SNE. 2. Geometric Deep Learning: The "Five Gs" of Symmetry What is it? Rather than treating every dataset as a raw list of numbers, Geometric Deep Learning designs neural networks that respect the underlying geometric domain and its symmetries equivariance . What does it study? - Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges: Convolutional networks respect translation symmetry on grids; graph neural networks respect permutation symmetry on graphs; mesh/manifold networks transport features along geodesics using local gauge frames. 3. Information Geometry: Measuring Distance Between Probability Distributions What is it? A parametric family of probability distributions MATH such as all 1D Gaussians MATH forms a smooth statistical manifold whose points are probability distributions. What does it study? - Fisher–Rao metric: Measures how distinguishable two nearby probability distributions are statistically—not how far apart their parameter numbers look on paper. - Natural gradient: Steepest descent measured with the Fisher–Rao ruler rather than the Euclidean ruler, making optimization invariant under reparametrization! --- Intuitive explanation Picture a Swiss roll : a flat two-dimensional sponge cake rolled into a spiral inside three-dimensional space MATH . Viewed as a raw cloud of MATH coordinates, points on adjacent layers look close together even though they belong to completely different parts of the cake. Unroll the spiral, and the entire dataset collapses cleanly onto a flat 2D rectangle. Between 2022 and 2025, Nick Whiteley, Annie Gray, and Patrick Rubin-Delanchy JRSS Series B gave the manifold hypothesis a rigorous statistical backbone: you do not need to assume nature magically places data onto a pre-built manifold. In a simple Latent Metric Model —random feature fields evaluated on hidden low-dimensional latent variables plus noise—high-dimensional data points automatically concentrate near a smooth low-dimensional manifold! Meanwhile, Michael Bronstein, Joan Bruna, Taco Cohen, and Petar Veličković unified modern deep learning under the “five Gs” — Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges —showing that successful neural architectures are discrete incarnations of the exact geometric structures you will build throughout this course. And in Information Geometry , moving in parameter space MATH is subtle: shifting the mean MATH by MATH when the standard deviation is MATH separates two bell curves completely, whereas shifting MATH by MATH when MATH barely changes the distribution at all! The Fisher–Rao metric captures that exact distortion. ! title: Optional: Recent Advances (2022–2026) — Curves, the Frenet Frame, and Curvature-Constrained Motion
content: Overview Close your eyes on a roller coaster in the pitch dark. Even without seeing a single inch of track ahead, your inner ear instantly knows two geometric numbers: how sharply the rail is bending sideways its curvature MATH and how aggressively the track is banking and corkscrewing out of the plane its torsion MATH . In Chapter 01, you learned how Jean Frédéric Frenet and Joseph Alfred Serret turned that visceral sensation into an orthonormal moving frame MATH riding along any space curve. What you might not expect is that those nineteenth-century equations are now running at hundreds of hertz inside modern robot arms , autonomous vehicles , and surgical catheter planners . Between 2022 and 2026, frameworks like Geometric Fabrics Van Wyk, Ratliff, and collaborators, IEEE RA-L / ICRA 2022 fused classical curve geometry and velocity-dependent Finsler metrics into real-time robot motion policies—turning bending, twisting, and obstacle avoidance into smooth geometric differential equations with provable stability. This optional lesson leaves the classical theory intact and shows how MATH , MATH , and MATH come alive in modern control and 3D vision. --- Key ideas: From Space Curves to Robot Motion Policies How does pure curve geometry translate into motors, torques, and obstacle avoidance? Three pillars connect them. 1. Differential Geometry of Space Curves: Moving Frames & Shape Rigidity What is it? Every regular arc-length curve MATH carries an intrinsic moving coordinate system: the unit tangent MATH , principal normal MATH , and binormal MATH . What does it study? - Fundamental Theorem of Space Curves: Up to rigid rotation and translation, a curve’s entire 3D shape is uniquely determined by just two scalar functions: curvature MATH and torsion MATH . - Osculating circle & turning radius: At each point, the curve kisses a circle of radius MATH —literally the tightest turning radius a vehicle or robot end-effector must execute. 2. Kinodynamic Control & Configuration Manifolds What is it? A 7-joint robot arm does not simply move a point in MATH ; its joint angles MATH trace a curve inside a 7-dimensional configuration manifold MATH . What does it study? - Curvature & acceleration budgets: Motors have finite torque limits. Because lateral acceleration grows as MATH , a path with a sudden spike in MATH forces either extreme torque or a drastic slowdown. - Motion policies: Rules MATH that continuously steer the robot toward a target while curving smoothly around obstacles. 3. Finsler Geometry & Geometric Fabrics 2021–2026 What is it? In standard Riemannian geometry, the cost of moving in a direction depends only on position MATH . In Finsler geometry , the metric can also depend on velocity MATH —allowing a robot to care strongly about an obstacle it is speeding toward, yet ignore an obstacle it is moving away from! What does it study? - Bending geodesics cleanly: Combining multiple behavioral rules stay within joint limits, avoid collisions, keep the wrist steady as geometric "fabrics" that still preserve a Lyapunov energy function , guaranteeing the robot never oscillates wildly or goes unstable. --- Intuitive explanation An industrial robot arm operates in the exact same "darkness" as our roller-coaster rider: its controller does not gaze at Euclidean space with human eyes—it senses joint angles, velocities, and task-space errors. If you ask a naive planner to minimize pure Euclidean distance to a goal, it will happily draw a sharp polygonal corner where MATH , demanding infinite acceleration and jarring the joints. Geometry insists that a physically feasible trajectory must live within a curvature budget MATH and a smooth rate of curvature change. Geometric Fabrics generalize classical Lagrangian mechanics by letting velocity-dependent Finsler metrics warp the "straight lines" geodesics of configuration space around obstacles, while keeping global energy dissipation intact. In medical imaging and computer vision, the exact same Frenet frame guides centerline extraction of blood vessels and airways: MATH runs along the lumen, MATH points directly into the tightest bend of the vessel wall, and MATH become invariant shape descriptors for detecting aneurysms or guiding robotic endoscopes. ! title: Optional: Recent Advances (2022–2026) — Implicit Surfaces and Gaussian Splatting
content:
Overview For half a century, if you wanted a computer to hold a 3D surface—a video-game character, a scanned statue, or a beating heart—you approximated it with a triangle mesh : millions of tiny flat triangles glued edge to edge. In Chapter 02, you learned the smooth mathematical truth underneath: a regular surface , defined either by local coordinate patches MATH or as the zero level set MATH of a smooth function with non-vanishing gradient, equipped at every point with a tangent plane and a unit normal . Between 2021 and 2025, computer graphics and 3D computer vision underwent a dramatic revolution by returning directly to those two classical definitions of a surface! 1. Neural Implicit Surfaces NeuS, Wang et al., NeurIPS 2021, and its 2022–2025 descendants : Instead of storing triangles, train a neural network to learn a smooth Signed Distance Function SDF MATH whose zero level set MATH is the exact 3D surface. 2. 3D & 2D Gaussian Splatting Kerbl et al., SIGGRAPH 2023; Huang et al., 2024 : Represent a scene as millions of optimizable, translucent Gaussian ellipsoids "splats" that render in real time—and then flatten those ellipsoids into 2D tangent disks hugging the true surface! This optional lesson reconnects those cutting-edge rendering breakthroughs directly to the implicit function theorem , unit normals , and tangent planes you just mastered in Chapter 02. --- Key ideas: Three Ways to Represent a Surface Every modern 3D vision pipeline is ultimately choosing between three classical geometric ways of describing a 2D surface inside MATH . 1. Parametric Patches vs. Implicit Level Sets What is it? - Parametric: A map MATH paints a 2D coordinate sheet onto 3D space like latitude and longitude on a globe . - Implicit: A scalar function MATH assigns a number to every point in MATH , and the surface is simply the contour MATH . What does it study? - Implicit Function Theorem: Guarantees that wherever MATH and MATH , the level set MATH is locally a smooth regular surface with unit normal MATH . - Signed Distance Functions SDFs : A special implicit function where MATH equals the exact shortest distance to the surface negative inside, positive outside , automatically obeying the Eikonal PDE MATH ! 2. Differentiable Volume Rendering NeRF & NeuS What is it? To reconstruct a 3D surface purely from 2D photographs, shoot a camera ray MATH through each pixel and integrate emitted color weighted by local opacity along the ray. What does it study? - Unbiased surface extraction: Converting an SDF MATH into a sharp volume density peaked precisely at the zero crossing MATH , so optimizing pixel colors automatically sculpts an accurate geometric surface. 3. Explicit Tangent Primitives 3D & 2D Gaussian Splatting What is it? A collection of localized 3D Gaussian blobs MATH with position MATH , covariance MATH , color, and opacity. What does it study? - From floating clouds to tangent planes: Pure 3D Gaussians render blazingly fast 100+ FPS , yet can float slightly off the true surface. 2D Gaussian Splatting 2024 collapses one axis of MATH to zero—turning each blob into an explicit tangent disk aligned with the surface’s normal! --- Intuitive explanation Remember pressing a stiff index card flat against a globe to visualize the tangent plane ? A neural SDF works from the outside in: it fills all of 3D space with a smooth scalar field—negative inside the object, positive outside—so the surface is the exact zero-contour where inside meets outside, and the gradient MATH points straight out as the normal vector. Gaussian Splatting works from the surface out: imagine tiling a sculpture with hundreds of thousands of tiny, softly feathered oval stickers, each with a center, an orientation, a color, and a transparency. From any camera angle, projecting "splatting" those stickers onto the screen paints a photorealistic image in milliseconds. Yet if the stickers are puffy 3D marshmallows floating in midair, the picture looks great while the underlying 3D geometry is lumpy. That is why 2024’s 2D Gaussian Splatting flattens every marshmallow into a razor-thin tangent disk—bringing computer graphics right back to Chapter 02’s stiff index card! ! Two centuries later, deep-learning researchers studying Graph Neural Networks GNNs ran into a baffling mystery: why do GNNs fail catastrophically when trying to pass information between distant nodes in a molecular graph or social network, even when you stack dozens of layers? In 2022–2023, two landmark papers Topping, Di Giovanni, Chamberlain, Dong, and Bronstein , ICLR 2022 ; and Nguyen, Nong, Nguyen, Ho, Osher, and Nguyen , ICML 2023 revealed that the culprit was pure intrinsic curvature ! On a curved surface, tangent spaces at different points are completely separate rooms—you cannot compare or add two vectors without a connection to transport one into the other's room. In 2019–2024 geometric deep learning, that exact problem reappeared under the name gauge equivariance and drove breakthroughs like Equiformer and EquiformerV2 .
